vuln_id: ARVO arvo:42264 / elfutils dwfl_segment_report_module note-parser wild read

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this exact staged vulnerable checkout, and its line map matches the saved ASan stack at `libdwfl/dwfl_segment_report_module.c:554` and `libdwfl/core-file.c:559`. Sample metadata names later still-vulnerable commit `bc14c148a6ad9b84bda428bd3bc75028515f0151`, which already contains extra partial note-length checks and therefore does not exactly match the staged source text reviewed here. The fixing commit remains `d844d1575522b5ad9ada0aa3c26105230a1c1884`.

classification.classification_note: Unchecked note-length arithmetic moves the `nh` cursor outside the note buffer; ASan reports the resulting sink as a wild-address `SEGV` caused by a READ at line 554 rather than as a typed heap or stack overflow.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in dwfl_segment_report_module in libdwfl where the notes filesz is not properly checked for excessive size. The reading of GElf_Nhdr does not verify for overflow at every step, and the size of the buildid bytes is not limited, potentially allowing for overflows and excessive memory usage.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged fix commit message
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 14,400-byte file `poc` (sha256 `06dea41b2b5abc69238a57b627d3b3842fe9c340fdf7e146b221d392778cef2e`), identified by `file` as an ELF64 LSB core file. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` writes those bytes unchanged to a temporary file, mmaps it with `elf_begin`, and calls `dwfl_core_file_report()`. On the reproduced crashing path, `dwfl_core_file_report()` reaches `dwfl_segment_report_module()` while sniffing a candidate in-memory ELF image. There, attacker-controlled PT_NOTE program-header fields provide the note-segment `offset`, `filesz`, and `align`, and attacker-controlled `GElf_Nhdr` fields provide `n_namesz` and `n_descsz`. In the staged vulnerable source, the note walker uses `while (filesz > len + sizeof (*nh))` as its loop guard, then advances `len` by `n_namesz` and `n_descsz` with alignment before validating those aligned spans, and the only check is `filesz < len + nh->n_descsz`. Because these additions are not overflow-checked at each step, `nh = notes + len` can step outside the note buffer while the loop still re-enters. The next `len += nh->n_namesz` at `libdwfl/dwfl_segment_report_module.c:554` then dereferences that invalid `nh`, and the saved sanitizer trace reports a wild-address READ `SEGV` from `dwfl_core_file_report`.

source.code: GElf_Word type = is32 ? p32[i].p_type : p64[i].p_type; GElf_Off offset = is32 ? p32[i].p_offset : p64[i].p_offset; GElf_Xword filesz = is32 ? p32[i].p_filesz : p64[i].p_filesz; GElf_Xword align = is32 ? p32[i].p_align : p64[i].p_align;
source.description: First project-code materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker state on the crashing path. `dwfl_segment_report_module()` decodes one attacker-controlled program header from the in-memory ELF image into the PT_NOTE selector and the `offset`/`filesz`/`align` values that drive the vulnerable note walker.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is the exact 14,400-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42264/poc` with sha256 `06dea41b2b5abc69238a57b627d3b3842fe9c340fdf7e146b221d392778cef2e`. It begins with ELF magic `7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01 00`, and `file` identifies it as an `ELF 64-bit LSB core file, x86-64`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` writes those bytes unchanged and calls `dwfl_core_file_report()`, which later reaches this program-header materialization inside `dwfl_segment_report_module()`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. On the re-entered loop iteration, `nh` no longer points inside the note buffer, and reading `nh->n_namesz` faults.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address ... The signal is caused by a READ memory access` at `dwfl_segment_report_module.c:554:30`.

root_cause.description: The note walker is driven by unchecked `len` arithmetic. It re-enters on `filesz > len + sizeof (*nh)` and then advances `len` by attacker-controlled `n_namesz` and `n_descsz` without validating the aligned spans before rebinding `nh`.
root_cause.note: The descendant fix commit `d844d1575522b5ad9ada0aa3c26105230a1c1884` rewrites this loop to use `filesz - len > sizeof (*nh)` and to validate aligned `namesz` and `descsz` before each addition, matching the missing obligation in the staged source.

tainted_value_origin.description: The malformed in-memory ELF program header supplies the note segment extent and alignment state that later govern `read_portion()`, `NOTE_ALIGN4/NOTE_ALIGN8`, and the loop bounds in the vulnerable note parser.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Those fields are materialized from the exact staged core-file witness after `dwfl_core_file_report()` has admitted the file and passed control into `dwfl_segment_report_module()`.

parser_admitted.code: int seg = dwfl_segment_report_module (dwfl, ndx, NULL, &dwfl_elf_phdr_memory_callback, elf, core_file_read_eagerly, elf, note_file, note_file_size, &r_debug_info);
parser_admitted.description: The saved crash stack proves the witness is admitted past the harness and core-file setup into the module-sniffing phase: `dwfl_core_file_report()` reaches this exact call to `dwfl_segment_report_module()` before the wild read occurs.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the exact staged core-file bytes to a temporary file, mmaps it with libelf, and calls `dwfl_core_file_report()`.
While reporting modules from the malformed core image, `dwfl_core_file_report()` enters its segment-sniffing loop and calls `dwfl_segment_report_module()`.
The module parser decodes an attacker-controlled PT_NOTE program header, reads the corresponding note bytes, and walks `GElf_Nhdr` entries using unchecked `len` arithmetic.

Because the note walker does not validate aligned `n_namesz` and `n_descsz` advances at each step, `nh` steps outside the note buffer and the next `nh->n_namesz` read at line 554 crashes with an ASan wild-address READ.

fine_trace.code: GElf_Word type = is32 ? p32[i].p_type : p64[i].p_type; GElf_Addr vaddr = is32 ? p32[i].p_vaddr : p64[i].p_vaddr; GElf_Xword memsz = is32 ? p32[i].p_memsz : p64[i].p_memsz; GElf_Off offset = is32 ? p32[i].p_offset : p64[i].p_offset; GElf_Xword filesz = is32 ? p32[i].p_filesz : p64[i].p_filesz; GElf_Xword align = is32 ? p32[i].p_align : p64[i].p_align;
fine_trace.note: From the candidate in-memory ELF image, the parser materializes one attacker-controlled program header as `type`, `offset`, `filesz`, and `align`. The crashing path depends on this header being a non-empty `PT_NOTE` segment, because those values become the note-buffer selector and bounds state for the vulnerable walker.

fine_trace.code: if (read_portion (&read_state, &data, &data_size, start, segment, note_vaddr, filesz)) continue; if (data_size != 0) filesz = data_size;
fine_trace.note: On the `PT_NOTE` path, the code reads the note segment from `start + offset` and then uses the returned byte count as the trusted segment extent if `read_portion()` supplied a resized buffer. The immediately following `ei_data` branch picks `notes` as either the raw bytes or an endian-converted copy, but in both cases the walker now trusts `filesz` as the number of valid bytes in `notes`.

fine_trace.code: const GElf_Nhdr *nh = notes; size_t len = 0; while (filesz > len + sizeof (*nh))
fine_trace.note: The note walker starts from the beginning of `notes` and uses `while (filesz > len + sizeof (*nh))` as its only re-entry condition. This guard itself is based on unchecked addition, and the later size advances rely on the same `len` state instead of validating each aligned note component before moving the cursor.

fine_trace.code: len += sizeof (*nh); note_name = notes + len; len += nh->n_namesz; len = align == 8 ? NOTE_ALIGN8 (len) : NOTE_ALIGN4 (len); note_desc = notes + len;
fine_trace.note: After stepping over the fixed note header, the parser adds attacker-controlled `nh->n_namesz` to `len` and aligns the result before any bounds or overflow check. `note_desc` is therefore derived from an unchecked aligned cursor.

The only guard runs after the unchecked name-size advance and tests raw `nh->n_descsz` against `len + nh->n_descsz`. It does not validate the aligned desc span and does not protect the addition itself from overflow, so malformed note sizes can still bypass the break.

fine_trace.code: len += nh->n_descsz; len = align == 8 ? NOTE_ALIGN8 (len) : NOTE_ALIGN4 (len); nh = (void *) notes + len;
fine_trace.note: When the incomplete guard in step 5 does not break, the parser advances `len` by attacker-controlled `nh->n_descsz`, aligns again, and rebinds `nh` to `notes + len`. On the crashing path, this new `nh` no longer points to a valid `GElf_Nhdr` inside the note buffer.

The next loop iteration still enters the body, and line 554 dereferences the out-of-bounds `nh` to fetch `nh->n_namesz`. The saved AddressSanitizer trace records this exact read as the crashing wild-address `SEGV`.

format.name: ELF64 core file
format.contract: Exact-match witness only: the saved 14,400-byte ELF64 LSB core file `poc` (sha256 `06dea41b2b5abc69238a57b627d3b3842fe9c340fdf7e146b221d392778cef2e`) that drives `dwfl_core_file_report()` into `dwfl_segment_report_module()` and makes the note walker re-enter with an invalid `nh`. Stage 02 does not establish a broader family of malformed note layouts beyond this witnessed file and the source-level requirement that the parsed PT_NOTE entry supplies note-header sizes that break the unchecked `len` arithmetic.
